description: We are Ecos del Humboldt, 4 students from Lima: 3 Environmental Engineering and 1 Fisheries Engineering. For The Earth Information Jukebox we will turn NASA ocean data (sea temperature, chlorophyll, El Niño) from the Peruvian coast into sound, so fishers and visually impaired people can "hear" the sea change. We bring Earth science, ocean and fisheries knowledge. Looking for: coding/web development, audio or music production, and video editing. ¡Hablamos español!
summary: Sound Bulletin of the Sea turns NASA Earth observation data into a weekly 30-second audio bulletin for small-scale fishers in five Peruvian ports: Paita, Chimbote, Callao, Pisco and Ilo. During the 2026 Coastal El Niño alert, ocean data stays locked in maps and numbers that most fishers never see. Our open Google Colab notebook downloads NASA POWER (sea temperature, wind, gusts, rain and humidity) and NASA JPL MUR SST at 1 km, compares each week with the 2001–2025 normal and turns it into a melody: the first note is the normal sea, the next seven are this week's days, and higher means warmer. Each bulletin adds a traffic-light alert, a 0–100 favorable-habitat index for five species based on their temperature ranges, a map of the 0–5 nautical-mile artisanal fishing zone and a ready-to-forward WhatsApp message. For 6–12 November 2026 every port was warmer than normal (+2.6 to +7.6 °C): conditions were unfavorable for anchovy and favorable for mahi-mahi, chub mackerel and skipjack tuna. It answers the Earth Information Jukebox challenge by making ocean data audible, local and actionable for people who listen rather than read charts. It is not an official warning and it does not detect fish schools.
details:
WHAT IT DOES

Sound Bulletin of the Sea is a weekly 30-second audio bulletin, map and WhatsApp message for small-scale fishers in five Peruvian ports: Paita, Chimbote, Callao, Pisco and Ilo. In 2026 Peru is under a Coastal El Niño alert, and ocean data stays locked in maps and numbers that most fishers never see. We make it audible.

HOW IT WORKS

1. Data: an open Google Colab notebook downloads NASA POWER daily data (sea skin temperature, wind, wind gusts, rain and humidity) and the 2001–2025 climatology, plus NASA JPL MUR SST at 1 km for the coastal zone. MODIS-Aqua data from NASA Giovanni (2003–2026) showed that 2026 broke monthly records in all three original ports.

2. Sound: each melody lasts about 8 seconds. The first note is the normal sea for the month and the next seven notes are this week's days, on a fixed pentatonic scale from 15 to 29 °C, so higher always means warmer and ports can be compared by ear. Wind is a soft breath, rain is small chimes. A traffic-light alert (green < +1 °C, yellow +1 to +3 °C, red > +3 °C) opens each bulletin.

3. Species: a 0–100 favorable-habitat index (trapezoid function) compares water temperature with the documented range of anchovy, jack mackerel, chub mackerel, mahi-mahi and skipjack tuna. One chime per favorable species, a low tone when anchovy moves away. Closed seasons (bonito, November) are flagged.

4. Map: 1 km points split into 0–5 nautical miles (reserved for artisanal fishing), 5–10 and 10–30 miles, with recommended areas, distance and direction from each port.

5. Delivery: the notebook outputs MP3 files, maps, a voice script and a ready-to-forward WhatsApp message. The website (https://ecos-del-humboldt.netlify.app/) lets anyone press "Start", choose a port and hear, see and share the bulletin.

RESULTS (6–12 Nov 2026)

Paita +7.6 °C, Chimbote +6.8 °C, Callao +6.0 °C, Pisco +5.7 °C (red) and Ilo +2.6 °C (yellow). Anchovy is outside its range in all ports; mahi-mahi, chub mackerel and skipjack find favorable water.

BENEFITS AND IMPACT

Fishers get information they can hear on any phone, without reading charts or knowing English. It helps them anticipate El Niño changes and look for opportunity species, while always pointing to official sources (IMARPE, PRODUCE, ENFEN).

TOOLS

Python (pandas, NumPy, SciPy, Matplotlib) in Google Colab, NASA POWER API, NOAA CoastWatch ERDDAP, NASA Giovanni, Audacity, HTML/CSS/JavaScript, Leaflet, Three.js, Netlify, ArcGIS Pro.

CREATIVITY AND HONESTY

The sea becomes music, and the music carries real data. We also tested chlorophyll-a as a "food" signal and rejected it: near the coast it showed no consistent link with warming. Limits we state openly: surface temperature only, 55 km NASA POWER grid, some species thresholds are team assumptions. The index shows favorable water conditions; it does not detect fish schools and it is not an official warning.
